newsitem.title: FRANCE: France holds seven suspected in Bordeaux bombing.
newsitem.headline: France holds seven suspected in Bordeaux bombing.

text.p: French police held seven men among 12 people rounded up on Thursday on suspicion of helping Corsican separatists bomb the mayoral office of Prime Minister Alain Juppe in Bordeaux two weeks ago, justice sources said.
The other five, the female companions of some of the men being held for questioning, were released, the sources said.

The interior ministry said police, including an elite anti-terrorist unit, swooped simultaneously on suspects in the town of Bonifacio, on the French Mediterranean island of Corsica, and around the southern mainland cities of Bordeaux and Marseille.
Two of the women had been brought in for questioning in Bonifacio, two near Bordeaux and one in Marseille, the sources said.
Police also seized weapons during Thursday's swoops.

The police action, the largest in years in connection with an upsurge in separatist violence in Corsica, appeared intended to demonstrate the prime minister's determination to firmly apply the law on the island.
Critics had predicted the Juppe government would not confront the separatist movement for fear of triggering spiralling guerrilla violence.
Police said unknown individuals sprayed a paramilitary police station with gunfire on Thursday afternoon. No one was hurt and no one immediately claimed responsibility for the shooting.

The "historic wing" of the Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) has claimed responsibility for the Bordeaux bombing, as well as for two later bombings of official buildings in the southern mainland town of Nimes.

The mainland attacks were a big escalation by separatists whose two-decade-old campaign for greater autonomy from France had been confined to hundreds of mostly small bombings in Corsica over the past few years.

Justice sources said that all seven of those held were close to the leader of the political wing of the FLNC, Francois Santoni, who was sentenced earlier this month in his absence to four months in jail for carrying guns.
Santoni is still in hiding. But among those arrested in Marseille were members of a family who have served as his bodyguards, the sources said.
One of those arrested in Corsica was Jean-Jacques Cantara, suspected of being one of Santoni's bodyguards, the justice sources said.
The Interior Ministry did not identify the detainees, but said they could have helped with the logistics for the attack on the Bordeaux city hall, which caused significant damage but no injuries.

The arrests were carried out on the orders of the country's senior anti-terrorist investigating judge, Jean-Louis Bruguiere, who was placed in charge of the probe when Juppe ordered a crackdown on Corsican guerrillas.
